items.q: The MN page figures contrast normal thin-walled capillaries with thick capillary walls, show granular IF, and label the schematic with effaced foot processes, thickened basement membrane, subepithelial deposits and:
items.exp: Schematic labels: podocyte with effaced foot processes, thickened BM, subepithelial deposits, spikes. (Book p769)

items.q: In the modified Ponticelli regimen for the 70% with NS, steroids are given on months:
Oral cyclophosphamide in the Ponticelli regimen is dosed at 2 mg/kg on months 2, 4, 6, and the regimen ends with:
items.exp: Oral cyclophosphamide (2 mg/kg) on months 2, 4, 6 → abrupt stop. (Book p769)

items.q: If there is no response to the Ponticelli regimen, the next agent written is:
items.exp: Rituximab: if no response to Ponticelli regimen. (Book p769)

items.q: The 30% asymptomatic MN arm is managed with ACE (−)/ARBs, salt restriction and protein at:
items.exp: 30% asymptomatic: ACE (−)/ARBs; salt restriction; 1 gm/kg/day protein. (Book p769)

items.q: Match each MN treatment item with its arm — 1) Modified Ponticelli regimen 2) Rituximab 3) ACE (−)/ARBs … A) 30% asymptomatic arm B) 70% with NS arm C) No response to Ponticelli
items.exp: 70% with NS → Ponticelli; no response → rituximab; 30% asymptomatic → ACE (−)/ARBs. (Book p769)

items.q: All of the following belong to the 30% asymptomatic MN arm EXCEPT:
items.exp: Steroids on months 1, 3, 5 belong to the Ponticelli regimen of the NS arm. (Book p769)

items.q: Which Ponticelli statement is TRUE as drawn?
opts: Steroids on months 1, 3, 5 alternate with cyclophosphamide on months 2, 4, 6 and the regimen stops abruptly
Steroids and cyclophosphamide run together every month
items.exp: Steroids months 1, 3, 5; cyclophosphamide months 2, 4, 6; abrupt stop. (Book p769)
